title: With one GOES-16 flux scale and one detection rule, Cycle 25 and Cycle 24 give equal M-flare rates at equal HMI flux; a GOES-15 offset and an SWPC listing change made the 1.15-1.21 residual
abstract: Question: earlier campaign work put the NOAA/SWPC flare list on the true GOES flux scale. At equal SDO/HMI magnetic flux, Cycle 25 still gave 1.15-1.21 times more M1+ flares than Cycle 24, mostly in multi-region complexes. Is this residual physical or instrumental? Method: we compared simultaneous 1-minute NCEI science-quality XRS-B fluxes of GOES-8 to GOES-19, put the SWPC list on the GOES-16 scale, applied one NOAA-like detection rule to one GOES-16-scale composite (2010-2026), and refitted the Poisson region-sum models of the prior work (sunspot number, SRS regions, HMI SHARP parameters) with paired 27-day block-bootstrap intervals. Results: GOES-15/GOES-16 = 0.930 (95% CI 0.927-0.932) at all flux levels in 2017-2019; GOES-14/GOES-16 = 0.865; GOES-16 to 19 agree within 2.3%. On the GOES-16 scale the Cycle 24 M1+ count rises by 8.9% (paired factor 1.089, 1.066-1.113). At the same daily activity, the GOES-R-era SWPC list has about 11% more M1+ events than a fixed rule, relative to Cycle 24 (0.89, 0.87-0.93); in Cycle 25, 3.4% of SWPC M1+ events are secondary peaks in the decay of larger flares, and in Cycle 24 none are. With one scale and one rule, Cycle 25/Cycle 24 at matched HMI flux, R and TOTUSJH is 1.00 (0.86-1.15) for M1+ and 0.99 (0.90-1.16) for C5+ flares. The multi-region excess falls to 1.08 (0.86-1.44) in a full-disk model without the SWPC flare-region assignment. Per sunspot number the M1+ excess becomes 1.14 (0.92-1.46). Limitations: Cycle 23 cannot be linked to the GOES-16 scale; the detection rule merges overlapping flares; Cycle 25 is incomplete; 100-300 bootstrap replicates.

citations.reason: We use its true-scale SWPC flare list and correct it to the GOES-16 scale.
We reuse its SRS, SHARP and assignment tables and model code; we find that its residual Cycle 25 excess and multi-region result are mostly instrumental and procedural.
Our result supports its conclusion that the per-sunspot excess comes from more flux per sunspot.
Five-cycle comparison on the old GOES scale.
